**Configuration and terms as top-level templates, safe operation without a separate admin workstation, a properly sized event log with guidance for central collection, and stable pseudonyms in reports.**

> The end-to-end lab validation of the 2.x scripts (L1-L20) is still in progress ([docs/VALIDATION.md](https://github.com/mayer-bautechnik/cloudsync-soa-toolkit/blob/v2.0.4/docs/VALIDATION.md)). Validate in your own lab first.

## Changed

- **The files you edit are templates at the top level:**
  - `SoaToolkit.config.example.psd1` (was `scripts\SoaToolkit.config.psd1`) and the new `SoaToolkit.terms.example.txt`.
  - Copy them to `SoaToolkit.config.psd1` / `SoaToolkit.terms.txt`. The copies are git-ignored and not part of the release zip, so extracting a new release never overwrites them.
  - Lookup order: `-ConfigPath`, then next to the script (deployed hosts, old layout), then the top level. Two configurations at once are refused.
- **Default `ReportPath` is `C:\SoaToolkitAdmin\Reports`** (was inside `DataPath`). It is created with access for Administrators and SYSTEM only.
- Report folders are named with seconds, so two runs within one minute no longer collide.

## Fixed

- **Running the admin scripts on a DC or agent host** (no separate admin workstation):
  - with `ReportPath` inside `DataPath`, the toolkit gMSA got modify rights on the install manifest, and the rollback deleted manifest and reports while it ran;
  - running the admin scripts from the deployed copy (`ScriptInstallPath`) let the rollback delete them.
  - Both layouts are now refused on toolkit hosts, with instructions. See [Without a separate admin workstation](https://github.com/mayer-bautechnik/cloudsync-soa-toolkit/blob/v2.0.4/docs/SETUP.md#21-without-a-separate-admin-workstation).
- **Event log `SoaToolkit`:** it was created with 512 KB and "overwrite older", so new events could be dropped when it was full. `DeployTasks` now sets `EventLogMaxSizeMB` (default 64) with "overwrite as needed"; new monitor check `EVENTLOG-SIZE`.

## New

- **Central collection** ([docs/OPERATIONS.md](https://github.com/mayer-bautechnik/cloudsync-soa-toolkit/blob/v2.0.4/docs/OPERATIONS.md#central-collection)):
  - Windows Event Forwarding with `SOA-Toolkit-Hosts` as subscription ACL and the optional `EventLogAllowWef`;
  - Azure Monitor Agent / DCR, both combined, SCOM;
  - alert recommendations and KQL, Tier-0 notes for the collector and Azure Arc.
- **Reports** (`Export-SoaReport.ps1`):
  - `SoaToolkit.terms.txt` is loaded automatically;
  - UPN suffixes (typically the public mail domain) are pseudonymized automatically;
  - pseudonyms are stable across reports (`-ResetPseudonyms` to start anew).
- The repository hygiene check uses the same terms file and scans only what git would publish.
- Design decisions D-21 to D-23.

## Upgrade from 2.0.3

1. Extract the release. Move your configuration from `scripts\SoaToolkit.config.psd1` to the top level as `SoaToolkit.config.psd1`.
2. If `ReportPath` is inside `DataPath` (the old default), move the folder - it contains `State\manifest.json` - and set the new path:
   ```powershell
   Move-Item C:\ProgramData\SoaToolkit\Reports C:\SoaToolkitAdmin\Reports
   ```
3. Optional: add `EventLogMaxSizeMB` / `EventLogAllowWef`, and create `SoaToolkit.terms.txt` from the template.
4. Update the hosts:
   ```powershell
   .\Install-SoaToolkit.ps1 -Step DeployTasks
   ```

Details: [CHANGELOG](https://github.com/mayer-bautechnik/cloudsync-soa-toolkit/blob/v2.0.4/CHANGELOG.md)

## Verify the download

Compare the SHA-256 of the asset with the digest GitHub shows next to it. The zip contains `SHA256SUMS.txt` for every file:

```powershell
Get-FileHash .\cloudsync-soa-toolkit-2.0.4.zip -Algorithm SHA256
Get-ChildItem -Recurse | Unblock-File
```

**Full changelog:** https://github.com/mayer-bautechnik/cloudsync-soa-toolkit/compare/v2.0.3...v2.0.4
